Title: Parallel add-to-cart requests are all persisted, none lost
Preconditions: Registered user, empty cart (auto-provisioned via API by the framework)
Test Data: 10 parallel POST /addtocart, unique line ids, Nexus 6
Steps:
1. Send 10 POST /addtocart in parallel, each with its own line id
2. POST /viewcart
Expected Result: All 10 requests return 200; cart has exactly 10 lines and their ids equal the ids sent (no lost writes).

Title: Replaying the same request in parallel creates exactly one line
Preconditions: Registered user, empty cart (auto-provisioned via API by the framework)
Test Data: 10 identical POST /addtocart with the same line id
Steps:
1. Send the same POST /addtocart (same id, same payload) 10 times in parallel
2. POST /viewcart
Expected Result: All requests return 200; cart has exactly 1 line with that id and product (replay is idempotent).

Title: Parallel deletes of the same line are safe
Preconditions: Registered user, empty cart (auto-provisioned via API by the framework); cart has 1 line
Test Data: 5 parallel POST /deleteitem with the same id
Steps:
1. Add 1 line
2. Send 5 POST /deleteitem for that line in parallel
3. POST /viewcart
Expected Result: No request errors; cart is empty; no exception from deleting an already-deleted line.

Title: Placing the order twice in parallel empties the cart once without errors
Preconditions: Registered user, empty cart (auto-provisioned via API by the framework); cart has 2 lines
Steps:
1. Add 2 products
2. Send 2 place-order requests in parallel
3. POST /viewcart
Expected Result: Both return 200; cart ends empty; no partial or duplicated state.

Title: Reusing an idempotency key with a different payload is rejected
Preconditions: Registered user, empty cart (auto-provisioned via API by the framework)
Test Data: Same line id: first Samsung galaxy s6, then Apple monitor 24
Steps:
1. POST /addtocart id=X prod_id=1
2. POST /addtocart id=X prod_id=10
3. POST /viewcart
Expected Result: Second request rejected (409/422) or ignored; cart keeps the original line with prod_id=1.
Actual Result / Notes: Known defect BUG-07: the line is silently overwritten with prod_id=10.

Title: Same user adding from two tabs at once keeps both items
Preconditions: User logged in, two tabs in one session
Test Data: Tab 1: Nexus 6, Tab 2: Sony vaio i5
Steps:
1. Open a different product in each tab
2. Click 'Add to cart' in both tabs at the same time
3. Check the cart
Expected Result: Cart contains both products exactly once.

Title: Double-clicking 'Add to cart' adds the product once
Steps:
1. Open the product page
2. Double-click 'Add to cart'
3. Wait for requests to settle; check the cart
Expected Result: Button is disabled / debounced after the first click; cart has 1 line.
Actual Result / Notes: Known defect BUG-08: two /addtocart requests are sent and 2 lines are created.

Title: Double-clicking 'Purchase' submits the order once
Preconditions: User logged in, cart has 1 item
Steps:
1. Open Place Order and fill the form
2. Double-click 'Purchase'
3. Count place-order requests
Expected Result: Exactly one order request is sent (payment-style double-charge protection).
Actual Result / Notes: Known defect BUG-09: two /deletecart requests are sent; on a real gateway this is a double charge.

Title: Successful login returns an Auth_token string
Preconditions: Registered user, empty cart (auto-provisioned via API by the framework)
Steps:
1. POST /login with valid credentials
2. Validate the body against loginSuccessSchema
Expected Result: HTTP 200, content-type application/json, body is a JSON string matching ^Auth_token: \S+$.

Title: Failed login returns the error contract
Preconditions: Registered user, empty cart (auto-provisioned via API by the framework)
Steps:
1. POST /login with a wrong password
2. POST /login with an unknown user
3. Validate each body against errorSchema
Expected Result: Body is exactly { errorMessage: string } with 'Wrong password.' / 'User does not exist.'.

Title: /addtocart succeeds with an empty body and /viewcart returns the typed line
Preconditions: Registered user, empty cart (auto-provisioned via API by the framework)
Expected Result: /addtocart: 200 with empty body. /viewcart: { Items: [{ cookie: string, id: string, prod_id: integer }] } with no extra fields.

Title: /viewcart of an empty cart returns an empty Items array
Preconditions: Registered user, empty cart (auto-provisioned via API by the framework)
Expected Result: Body matches viewCartSchema and Items is [].

Title: Malformed token returns the error contract on /addtocart and /viewcart
Steps:
1. POST /addtocart with a malformed token
2. POST /viewcart with a malformed token
Expected Result: Body matches errorSchema with 'Bad parameter, token malformed.'; nothing is stored.

Title: Errors are reported with a 4xx status code
Steps:
1. POST /login with an unknown user
2. Check the HTTP status
Actual Result / Notes: Known defect BUG-10: every error is HTTP 200 with an errorMessage body.

Title: /addtocart rejects a product id that does not exist
Preconditions: Registered user, empty cart (auto-provisioned via API by the framework)
Actual Result / Notes: Known defect BUG-11: the line is stored with prod_id=999999.

Title: Checkout flow smoke: 1 VU for 30 s
Preconditions: k6 installed; 1 user signed up in setup()
Steps:
1. npm run perf:smoke
2. Flow per iteration: login → add to cart → verify cart → place order → verify cart emptied
Expected Result: All thresholds pass: http_req_failed <1%, p95 <2 s, p99 <4 s, per-step p95 <1.5 s, checks >99%, business_errors <1%, checkout p95 <6 s.
Actual Result / Notes: Run 13 Oct 2026: 11 iterations, 100% checks, p95 547 ms — all thresholds passed.

Title: Checkout flow load: ramp to 5 VUs, hold 1 min
Preconditions: k6 installed; PEAK_VUS users signed up in setup()
Steps:
1. npm run perf:checkout
2. Same flow as TC-K6-001
Expected Result: Same thresholds as TC-K6-001 under sustained load.
Actual Result / Notes: Run nightly / on demand in the CI 'load' job.

Title: Checkout flow spike: 1 → 20 VUs in 10 s, hold 30 s, recover
Preconditions: k6 installed; 20 users signed up in setup()
Steps:
1. npm run perf:spike
2. Watch latency and errors during the ramp and after recovery
Expected Result: Same thresholds as TC-K6-001 during and after the spike; latency returns to baseline after ramp-down.
Actual Result / Notes: Run 13 Oct 2026: 301 orders, checks 99.90%, p95 557 ms, p99 999 ms, http_req_failed 0.06% (1/1525) — all thresholds passed.
